claim: Replay-derived binary tape macros were mined from live tactic-route proposal journals and compared fail-closed against the ordinary parameterized primitive catalog from two distinct authenticated native frontiers and deterministic seeds.

establishes: live proposal journals are consumed by replay-fragment discovery
candidate tapes remain exact controller inputs rather than a second action language
comparative promotion evidence is native-executed across distinct states and seeds
proposal, comparison, lifecycle, and source-transition provenance round-trip through a versioned CBOR and zstd binary registry
validation simulation, restore, preparation, persistence, and wall time are reported
does_not_establish: reuse of a promoted tactic in a later learning decision
cold replay of a promoted tactic
improvement against the authenticated 125-tick Ordon incumbent

implementation.registry_encoding: versioned checksummed envelope containing zstd-compressed CBOR; tapes use the canonical binary InputTape encoding

verdict: The comparative gate worked and refused promotion because no candidate beat the best primitive baseline across both sealed comparisons. This is negative promotion evidence, not P4 acceptance.
